findings.title: Rebalances reuse a pool whose workers have already been stopped
findings.body: The queue pool is created once in the factory and reused for every strategy returned by create_with_partitions(), but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/join() shuts that pool down. When Arroyo replaces the strategy after a partition rebalance, the new strategy therefore receives the old, stopped pool. Its submissions either fail because the queues are shut down (and are then marked completed by the exception handler) or accumulate without any workers. Create a fresh pool and offset tracker for each strategy assignment rather than sharing their lifecycle across strategies.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown abandons queued work and stops commits before draining
findings.body: Setting worker.shutdown to True makes each worker exit after its current item, even when its queue still contains accepted messages; queue.shutdown(immediate=False) does not override that loop condition. In addition, strategy.close() stops the commit thread before shutting down the workers, so work completed during shutdown never receives a final commit. Thus close()/join() neither drains accepted work nor commits its final completed offsets, causing replay and potentially duplicate uptime side effects on shutdown or rebalance. Graceful close should stop accepting submissions, drain workers, and commit the final safe offsets before returning.

findings.title: Unbounded queues remove consumer backpressure
findings.body: Each work queue is constructed without a maxsize, and submit() always accepts messages without raising MessageRejected or otherwise limiting in-flight work. If processing falls behind Kafka ingestion, especially when a slow result blocks one queue, the consumer continues retaining decoded results and original messages indefinitely. The offset tracker also retains later completed offsets behind that slow item. This can exhaust process memory rather than applying the advertised backpressure. Bound total in-flight work and reject submissions until capacity becomes available.
